text:
Berkly Catton is having the kind of second season Seattle hoped for when it drafted him. He scored three in Thursday's 5-1 win over Vancouver, a night when the Kraken put 43 shots on the Canucks, and he has 11 points in his last 10 games. That's well above the 5.7 the chances behind them would usually produce, so enjoy it, but don't bank all of it.

That's the honest read on the whole team. At 10-8-1 and 21 points, Lane Lambert's Kraken sit in the race, yet they've had only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against). They've scored about eight more goals than those chances would predict, and our numbers have them roughly four points ahead of what their play has earned. Their playoff chances sit near 30%.

The good news lives on one line. Kaapo Kakko, Shane Wright and Catton have broken even on chances and outscored opponents 8-6. The Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann trio has been the opposite, with 39% of the chances, and McMann has 2 points in 10 games.

Jagger Firkus, the WHL's 2024 player of the year, made his NHL debut in the Global Series finale in Finland, which is a nice story for a team that needs young legs. What we'd watch is the Pacific stretch ahead: if the shot share doesn't climb, the shooting luck will eventually run out.
headline: Catton's cat trick, and a gap underneath
